What It Is: 10-month team-based national service for adults 18-24; crews deploy to nonprofits, federal agencies, and disaster sites for environmental stewardship, infrastructure, and community development.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Modest living allowance (AmeriCorps states 'equivalent of ~$12.60/hr' for NCCC package in 2023; FY2026 exact dollar unverified) + communal housing + meals + travel covered + limited health benefit + Segal Education Award of ~$7,395 upon completion. End-of-service cash stipend alternative ~$1,800.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application only (americorps.gov). No recruiter commission or referral bonus.

Status 2026: ACTIVE — accepting applications for FEMA Corps (apply July-Oct 2026), Forest Corps (Nov 2026-Mar 2027), Traditional Corps (Mar-Jun 2027). Program survived 2025 AmeriCorps funding cuts; NCCC FEMA Corps members were briefly demobilized in 2025 but program restored under FY2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act (P.L. 119-75, Feb 2026).

What It Is: Specialized 10-month track within NCCC; members work alongside FEMA staff on disaster preparedness, mitigation, response, and recovery. Must be U.S. citizen.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Same NCCC compensation package as Traditional Corps: living allowance (FY2026 exact dollar unverified; compensation package equivalent approx. $12.60/hr per 2023 data) + communal housing + meals + all program travel + limited health benefit + Segal Education Award ~$7,395 upon completion.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application only.
Location: Nationwide; may train at FEMA Emergency Training Center (Emmitsburg MD) or FEMA Incident Workforce Academy (Anniston AL)
Stage: Gap year / post-high school or post-college
Selectivity: Moderate; subset of 500 total NCCC slots
Status 2026: ACTIVE — applications open July 1 – Oct 19, 2026; service Jan/Feb – Nov 2027.

What It Is: 10-month NCCC track partnered with the U.S. Forest Service; crews work on wildfire risk mitigation, fuels reduction, reforestation, and resource management. Must be U.S. citizen.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Same NCCC compensation package: living allowance (FY2026 exact dollar unverified) + communal housing + meals + travel + limited health benefit + Segal Education Award ~$7,395 upon completion.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application only.
Stage: Gap year / post-high school or post-college
Selectivity: Moderate; subset of 500 total NCCC slots
Status 2026: ACTIVE — applications open Nov 2026 – Mar 2027; service May/June 2027 – Apr 2028.

What It Is: One-year anti-poverty capacity-building program; members serve full-time with nonprofits and public agencies to expand program capacity, not deliver direct service. Placements nationwide.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Living allowance based on 105% of federal poverty level for single person in service area (varies by county; e.g., one Michigan listing showed $1,119/biweekly pre-tax ≈ $29,100/yr) + upon completion: Segal Education Award $7,395 OR cash stipend ~$1,800 (choose one). Health insurance, student loan forbearance with interest paid, childcare assistance if eligible.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application through My AmeriCorps portal.
Status 2026: ACTIVE — program operating. Note: ~80% of AmeriCorps State & National grants were terminated April 2025 but courts ordered restoration and FY2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act (P.L. 119-75) restored funding. VISTA grants were separately maintained and less disrupted.

What It Is: Federal grants fund hundreds of nonprofit programs that place AmeriCorps members in community service roles across education, disaster, economic opportunity, veterans, and environment focus areas.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: FY2026 minimum full-time living allowance: $20,400/yr ($12/hr) per FY2025 policy (FY2026 rate unverified from AmeriCorps.gov directly; FY2025 set at $20,400). Maximum living allowance up to $33,200+/yr depending on program/location. Segal Education Award $7,395–$7,397 upon full-term completion. Health insurance for full-time members.
Referral / Partner Economics: None for participants — direct application. Individual grantee organizations sometimes hire campus recruiters (paid staff positions) but no commission paid to outside referrers.
Stage: Gap year / post-high school or post-college
Selectivity: Varies by program; overall thousands of openings annually
Status 2026: ACTIVE WITH CAUTION — approximately 41% of AmeriCorps grants were terminated April 25, 2025 by Trump administration. Federal court injunctions (June 2025) and FY2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act (P.L. 119-75, Feb 2026) restored substantial funding. Program operating in FY2026 but future uncertain; Trump FY2027 budget proposed eliminating AmeriCorps entirely.

What It Is: AmeriCorps operator placing full-time corps members as student success coaches in high-need urban K-12 schools across 29 U.S. cities; 11-month term, 1,700 service hours.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Biweekly living stipend (pre-tax) varies by city for 2025-2026 school year: $907 (Columbia SC/New Hampshire) to $1,386 (Bay Area) biweekly. Annualized range approx. $23,600-$36,000/yr. Plus: health/dental/vision insurance, $500 relocation allowance (50+ miles), Segal Education Award $7,397 upon completion, student loan forbearance, childcare if eligible.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at cityyear.org. No affiliate or recruiter commission.
Location: 29 cities nationwide including Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Miami, Sacramento, Seattle, Washington DC, and more
Stage: Gap year / post-high school or post-college
Selectivity: Moderate; several thousand corps members annually
Status 2026: ACTIVE — City Year confirmed operating for 2025-2026 year with full stipend tables posted.

What It Is: 2-year paid teaching corps; corps members are hired as full-time teachers by partner school districts and charter networks in low-income communities. Not an AmeriCorps stipend program — members earn a teacher salary.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: District salary of $32,000-$72,000/yr depending on region (paid by school district). TFA also provides: summer training living stipend $3,000-$6,500, need-based grants and loans, access to grad school scholarships. No Segal Education Award (not AmeriCorps-linked).
Referral / Partner Economics: None for outside referrers. TFA operates a campus recruiting infrastructure with paid TFA staff; no commission to external counselors or agents.
Stage: Post-college (most corps members are recent graduates; some career changers)
Status 2026: ACTIVE — continuing operations.

What It Is: 10-month AmeriCorps apprenticeship program placing young adults 18-30 at nonprofit organizations 4 days/week plus weekly leadership training. 1,700 service hours. $6.6M AmeriCorps grant announced July 2026 for 288 apprenticeships.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: $22,000 total living stipend (taxable) over 10-month full-time term (confirmed for 2025-2026 at Pittsburgh site). Part-time: $8,500. Plus: health care, child care subsidy, monthly bus pass, Segal Education Award $7,395 upon completion, student loan forbearance.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at publicallies.org.
Location: Multiple cities nationwide (Milwaukee, Chicago, Cincinnati, Albuquerque, and others); 288 positions in FY2026 grant
Stage: Gap year / post-high school or early career
Status 2026: ACTIVE — received $6.6M AmeriCorps grant July 2026 to place 288 apprentices.

What It Is: AmeriCorps program placing coaches in high schools and colleges to help low-income students prepare for and succeed in college. 2026-2027 service year starts August 2026.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Full-time First-Year Coach: $23,040/yr ($1,001.74 biweekly) in some locations; $25,800/yr ($1,121.73 biweekly) in other locations. Three-quarter-time: ~$20,900-$23,000/yr. Plus: education award (Segal), healthcare. Final 2026-2027 compensation to be posted Jan 2027.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at collegepossible.org.
Location: Minnesota (Twin Cities), Oregon (Portland), Wisconsin (Milwaukee), Nebraska (Omaha), Pennsylvania (Philadelphia), and other states
Status 2026: ACTIVE — Note: College Possible Philadelphia closed during 2025 AmeriCorps funding chaos; other sites confirmed operating.

What It Is: AmeriCorps program placing full-time literacy intervention coordinators and community engagement leads in elementary school reading centers across 10+ states. Members tutor students and manage volunteer tutors.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Living allowance varies by region: approx. $22,100 (Tulsa, SC) to $28,100 (NYC, SF Bay Area, Silicon Valley) for the service year (2023-24 figures; 2026 unverified). Plus: $500 mid-year bonus + $3,000 end-of-year bonus + medical/dental/vision + transit reimbursement $127/mo + Segal Education Award ~$7,395.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at readingpartners.org.
Location: Washington DC, Maryland, New Jersey, California, Texas, Minnesota, Washington state, Oklahoma, South Carolina, New York, Colorado
Stage: Gap year / post-high school or post-college
Status 2026: ACTIVE — program continued operating through 2025 funding disruptions.

What It Is: AmeriCorps State & National operator placing members at local Habitat affiliates to coordinate construction volunteers, assist home builds, and strengthen organizational capacity. Full-time 10.5-12 month positions.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Living allowance: minimum $18,700 for full-time 10.5-month term; 12-month positions range $24,893-$40,757 depending on location. Some affiliates add housing stipend (e.g., Bay Area EBSV: additional $1,500-$1,800/mo toward rent). Segal Education Award ~$7,395 upon completion. Health coverage.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — apply at habitat.org or through My AmeriCorps. No external referral fee.
Location: Nationwide at local Habitat affiliates (Twin Cities, Bay Area, and many others confirmed for 2026)
Status 2026: ACTIVE — Twin Cities Habitat for Humanity confirmed 2026 positions active and accepting rolling applications. Program survived 2025 AmeriCorps disruptions.

Program: Green City Force (AmeriCorps State & National operator)
What It Is: 6-10 month AmeriCorps workforce development program for NYCHA/affordable housing residents 18-24 in New York City; members serve 4 days/week in green economy service projects and 1 day/week in career training.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Monthly stipend (exact FY2026 dollar amount unverified on operator's site) + unlimited monthly MetroCard + Segal Education Award upon completion + wraparound support services + career services.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at greencityforce.org. No affiliate commission.
Selectivity: Moderate; limited to NYC NYCHA/affordable housing residents
Status 2026: ACTIVE — program website recruiting year-round for 2026.

What It Is: Federal volunteer program placing Americans abroad for 27 months (2-3 months training + 24 months service) in education, health, agriculture, environment, youth development, and economic development sectors.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Monthly living allowance (amount set country-by-country to match local modest lifestyle; not a U.S. wage). Free housing. Round-trip flights. Paid vacation. Readjustment allowance of $375/month of service paid as lump sum at completion (~$10,500 for full 27 months). Medical/dental during service.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at peacecorps.gov. No affiliate or recruiter commission.
Location: ~60 countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America, Eastern Europe, Pacific Islands
Stage: Post-college; minimum age 18, no upper limit
Status 2026: ACTIVE — Peace Corps continues operating. Note: Peace Corps has faced its own federal budget pressures under Trump administration but was not terminated as of August 2026.

What It Is: California state program (not AmeriCorps) providing paid conservation service and job training for youth 18-25. Residential and non-residential options. Crews do forestry, wildfire, flood control, trails, and disaster response.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: $2,814/month stipend at entry level (before taxes). Residential members: $500/month maintenance fee deducted, net $2,314/month. Promotional levels: $2,904 (first promotion), $2,967 (second promotion). Scholarships up to $8,000/year. Emergency Excess Time paid separately. Health benefits.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at ccc.ca.gov. California state program.
Location: California statewide (residential centers and non-residential community crews)
Stage: Gap year / early career; 18-25 years old
Selectivity: Low; open to all income levels, California resident preferred
Status 2026: ACTIVE — California state program, not dependent on federal AmeriCorps grants.

What It Is: California AmeriCorps fellowship placing 400 fellows with host partners in underserved communities statewide for 11 months; focus on urban greening, organic waste recovery, and wildfire resiliency. State-level successor to terminated federal American Climate Corps.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: $35,250 living allowance (pre-tax) paid biweekly over 11 months. Combined $10,000 education award (Segal Education Award + California for All Education Award) upon completion. Student loan forbearance with interest paid. Childcare assistance. SNAP eligibility. Up to $300 professional development stipend.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at caclimateactioncorps.org. California Volunteers / AmeriCorps program.
Status 2026: ACTIVE — applications open May 1-July 31, 2026 for September 21, 2026 start. State-funded successor to terminated federal American Climate Corps (terminated by executive order Jan 2025).

What It Is: AmeriCorps State & National program operated by Washington State Department of Ecology; conservation crews do habitat restoration, trail construction, invasive species control, and environmental education. Ages 18-25.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Biweekly stipend (exact amount unverified from operator page) + health insurance + AmeriCorps Education Award upon completion: $7,395 (full term), $5,176.50 (three-quarter term), $1,956.35 (quarter term) + student loan forbearance with interest paid.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — apply at ecology.wa.gov/wcc.
Duration: Varies: full-term (~9 months), three-quarter, or quarter-term; summer positions June 8 – Sept 10, 2026
Status 2026: ACTIVE — recruiting 25+ summer 2026 positions (June-Sept 2026) for trail maintenance and habitat restoration.

What It Is: AmeriCorps conservation corps based in Montana; field crews and individual placements do trail construction, habitat restoration, wildfire mitigation, and natural resource projects across Montana and surrounding states. Ages 18+.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Field Support Technician (seasonal, 2026): $1,440 biweekly (before taxes) + $3,697.50 Education Award + free health insurance. Conservation Fellow positions: $750 biweekly + $2,474 Education Award + free health insurance. Member Assistance Program. Public Lands Service Corps federal hiring preference.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — apply at mtcorps.org.
Location: Montana and surrounding states (Idaho, Wyoming, the Dakotas)
Duration: Seasonal (spring through fall) or year-round for some roles; Conservation Fellow: part-year
Status 2026: ACTIVE — accepting 2026 season applications; some roles filled, others still open as of mid-2026.

What It Is: Largest youth conservation organization; places teens and young adults in paid conservation internships and crew positions at national parks, forests, and urban green spaces. Many positions carry AmeriCorps education awards.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Varies by position: many SCA positions offer stipends (amount varies; unverified specific FY2026 dollar from operator site). Some positions also carry AmeriCorps Segal Education Award. Academic credit available. Benefits include hands-on training and housing for residential positions.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — direct application at thesca.org.
Location: Nationwide: national parks, forests, marine sanctuaries, and urban green spaces in 30+ states
Duration: Varies: 12-week summer positions to 52-week individual placements
Stage: High school age through young adult; teens (15+) and adults 18+
Status 2026: ACTIVE — posting 2026 seasonal positions. Some SCA positions linked to AmeriCorps grants may have been affected by 2025 cuts.

What It Is: AmeriCorps conservation corps program of Conservation Legacy operating in Arizona; field crews do habitat restoration, trail work, invasive species removal, and watershed projects on public lands.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Living allowance (Conservation Legacy Individual Placement listings confirm stipend + living allowance for 2026 term; exact AZCC amount unverified on azcorps.org). AmeriCorps Education Award ~$7,395 (full term) upon completion. Health insurance.
Referral / Partner Economics: None — apply at azcorps.org or conservationlegacy.org.
Location: Arizona (and public lands in surrounding Southwest)
Duration: Varies: seasonal crews (3-6 months) and individual placements (12 months)
Status 2026: ACTIVE — Individual Placement listings show 01/01/2026-12/31/2026 terms open across AZ, CO, NC, NM, VA, TN, WV.

What It Is: Work-exchange network matching volunteers (WWOOFers) with organic farms for roughly 25 hrs/week of farm labor in return for room and board. No cash changes hands between host and WWOOFer. Minimum age 18.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Membership fee: $40/year solo, $65/year joint (confirmed from wwoof.net membership-terms PDF, March 2026). Hidden costs: participant pays all transport to/from farm, must carry travel/medical insurance. Flights can add $200–$1,500+. Zero farm stipend.
Referral / Partner Economics: None published. WWOOF USA does not operate an affiliate or referral program.
Location: USA (1,100+ host farms across all 50 states)
Selectivity: Low — open application; hosts choose whom to accept
Status 2026: Active. Note: WWOOF USA requires insurance; unvetted placements carry real safeguarding risk — no background checks on hosts. Exploitation incidents documented in press.

What It Is: Same WWOOF model but covers 80+ countries without their own national organization. One membership unlocks hosts across all those countries. Managed by the Federation of WWOOF Organizations (FoWO).
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Membership fee: $35/year (individual), $55 dual (confirmed help.wwoof.net March 2026 table). Same hidden costs as WWOOF USA: flights, visa, insurance.
Referral / Partner Economics: None published.
Location: Worldwide (80+ countries without a national WWOOF org)
Status 2026: Active. Same safeguarding caveats as WWOOF USA.

What It Is: Country-specific WWOOF memberships. Italy: €40 individual, €80 dual. France: €28/€34. Germany: €35/€55. Each is a separate purchase and covers only that country.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Italy €40, France €28, Germany €35 (individual, annual, verified help.wwoof.net March 2026). Must add flights — typically $600–$1,200 round-trip from US — plus insurance. All-in first year: roughly $800–$1,400+ per country. Reclassify as YOU PAY for first year abroad.
Referral / Partner Economics: None published.
Status 2026: Active. Same safeguarding caveats. WWOOF Italy has had documented labor-law compliance issues.

What It Is: Global work-exchange directory with 50,000+ host opportunities in 170+ countries. Volunteers offer 4–5 hrs/day of help (hostel work, teaching, farm, care) in return for room and board. Platform only; individual hosts set their own terms.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Membership: US$69/year solo, US$79/year couple (confirmed workaway.info signup page 2026). Flights and insurance are additional and can easily total $1,000+. Some hosts charge an extra daily fee — not standard but present.
Referral / Partner Economics: Active affiliate program: monthly PayPal commission per successful referral. Member referral tier: 3 months free membership per referral (up to 2 years free with 8 referrals). After 8 referrals, invited to formal Affiliate program with cash commission. Exact commission rate not publicly disclosed — described as 'monthly commission via PayPal'. Source: workaway.info/en/community/affiliates and workaway.info/en/stories/travel-long-term-free.
Duration: Typically weeks to 3 months per placement
Status 2026: Active. Safeguarding risk: unvetted hosts; incidents of labor exploitation and personal safety issues documented. Background checks not mandatory. Orphanage-style placements exist — now widely condemned by child-safeguarding bodies.

What It Is: Work-exchange platform with 50,000+ verified host positions globally. Emphasizes safety with WP Safeguard (emergency accommodation reimbursement up to $59–$399 depending on plan) and double-blind reviews. Max 32 volunteer hours/week.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Membership: US$59/year solo, US$69/year couples (verified worldpackers.com/get_verified, 2026). Premium 'Pack Plus' plans: US$139–$159. Flights and insurance additional. Some hosts charge extra collaboration fee — verify before confirming. Referral affiliate discount: Affiliates give users US$10 off first purchase.
Referral / Partner Economics: Guru Program: members with 2+ positive reviews earn cash commission per conversion using their Expert code. One testimonial cites US$1,200+ earned. Blogger program pays US$50–$160 per approved article. Creator program pays monthly for social media content. Affiliate promo codes give referred buyers US$10 off. Source: worldpackers.com/programs.
Duration: Typically 1 week to 3 months per placement
Status 2026: Active. WP Safeguard adds meaningful protection vs other platforms.

What It Is: Peer-to-peer work-exchange directory. Helpers offer ~4 hrs/day in return for accommodation and meals. Covers farms, homestays, hostels, boats, ranches in 140+ countries. One of the oldest platforms (launched early 2000s).
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Premier helper upgrade: €20 for 2 years (verified helpx.net/faq and helpx.net/registerchoice, 2026). No separate annual fee after that. Flight/insurance costs additional. Hosts listed for free. Very low platform cost.
Referral / Partner Economics: None published.
Selectivity: Low — direct contact; no formal vetting
Status 2026: Active. No background checks. Free-tier hosts can see helpers but premium required to initiate contact. Lower safeguarding infrastructure than Worldpackers.

What It Is: Work-exchange and volunteer-stay platform focused on 'Hospitality First' model. 2,500+ vetted hosts in 100+ countries — all screened and approved by the HelpStay team before listing.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Annual membership: €42.99 solo, €51.99 couple/friends (confirmed helpstay.com FAQ pages and comparison sources, 2026). Some hosts charge additional daily fees (example listings show €22–€25/day for some placements). Flights and insurance extra.
Referral / Partner Economics: None publicly documented.
Status 2026: Active. User reviews note interface less polished than competitors; host vetting more selective than HelpX but complaints about consistency.

What It Is: Pet-sitting exchange platform: sitters care for pets and homes of absent owners, with free accommodation provided in return. No cash changes hands between homeowner and sitter. Both parties pay separate annual memberships.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Sitter membership: approximately US$129 (Basic), US$189 (Standard), US$259 (Premium) per year (unverified exact USD sitter tier — pricing page showed Pet Parent tiers US$149/229/299; sitter tiers differ). Pet Parent Basic US$149/year confirmed. No sitter is paid; no homeowner pays sitter. Flights to reach sits are participant's own cost — this can be significant.
Referral / Partner Economics: Refer-a-Friend: active members earn 2 months free per friend who joins; referred friend gets 25% off their membership (confirmed trustedhousesitters.com/blog/news/referring-a-friend-how-it-works, 2022 — program still active per forum posts Feb 2026). Affiliate program for content creators with 5,000+ followers: competitive commission via Impact.com, 30-day cookie. Details: trustedhousesitters.com/pages/affiliates/.
Location: Worldwide (sits concentrated in USA, UK, Europe)
Selectivity: Moderate — homeowners choose sitters from applicants
Status 2026: Active. Well-established safeguarding: background checks available, reviews system. Sitters must transport themselves to each sit.

What It Is: Print and online newsletter (since 1983) listing property caretaking and house-sitting positions. Many positions offer rent-free living in exchange for maintenance, caretaking, or housesitting labor. Published bimonthly; email updates several times a week.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Subscription: $39.95/year (confirmed caretaker.org, July/August 2026 Issue #262 active). Some positions pay a small salary; others are room-only. Positions are highly varied — some include stipend, vehicle, utilities. Flights to remote positions are own cost.
Referral / Partner Economics: None published.
Status 2026: Active. No position vetting by Gazette — due diligence is participant's own responsibility (per their Terms of Use).

What It Is: World's largest online crew-boat matching network. Crew members offer sailing labor in return for a berth (free accommodation aboard). Positions range from recreational passages to longer delivery trips. Free to register; Premium required to exchange contact details.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Registration is free. Premium membership required for messaging (pricing not publicly listed on main page; approximately US$50–$100/year per external sources). Many positions are unpaid berth-for-crew; some ask crew to contribute to fuel/food. Flights to departure port are own cost. Crew may contribute to provisions on recreational passages — verify terms before accepting.
Referral / Partner Economics: None published.
Status 2026: Active. Safeguarding risk: at-sea situations require careful vetting — the site explicitly warns users to ask extensive questions before boarding.

What It Is: Open-work visa for US citizens to live and work in Australia for 12 months (extendable to 3 years via regional work). Note: US citizens use subclass 462, NOT 417 — a common error in most guides. Requires tertiary education evidence (at least 2 years of university).
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Visa fee AUD $840 (~USD $545) paid upfront. Proof of funds required. Typical wages AUD $24–30/hr (minimum wage AUD $24.10/hr in 2026). Hospitality and farm work earns AUD $2,500–4,500/mo. Net positive over a 12-month stay by $15,000–30,000 AUD after costs.
Referral / Partner Economics: No formal affiliate scheme for the visa. Third-party agents (not endorsed by Home Affairs) charge AUD $200–500 for application help. Working holiday placement agencies (farm, hospitality) charge employers AUD $0–500 finder fees, unpublished.
Location: Australia (any region; regional work required for year 2/3 extension)
Duration: 12 months; extendable to 24 months (regional work) or 36 months
Selectivity: Low — apply online, no interview; cap applies but historically generous for US
Status 2026: OPEN to US citizens. Age 18–30 at application. US is NOT eligible for 417.

What It Is: The more commonly advertised Australian working holiday visa. Covers UK, Ireland, Canada, and many European passport holders. US citizens are NOT eligible — this is the single most common error in gap-year advice.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: N/A for US citizens — CLOSED to US passport holders. Use 462 instead.
Referral / Partner Economics: N/A
Status 2026: CLOSED to US citizens. US is ineligible for subclass 417.

Program: New Zealand Working Holiday Visa (US scheme)
What It Is: Open-work visa to live and work anywhere in New Zealand for 12 months. US scheme is uncapped — apply any time, no waiting for an annual quota opening.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Visa fee NZD $770 + NZD $100 IVL levy (~USD $530 total). Proof of NZD $4,200 funds required. Minimum wage NZD $23.15/hr (2026). Typical hospitality/farm wages NZD $2,500–4,000/mo. Net positive over 12 months by NZD $10,000–25,000 after setup costs.
Referral / Partner Economics: No official affiliate. Working holiday starter packages (accommodation + bank setup) sold by operators like KILROY for GBP $200–400 targeting European holders; similar services target US holders.
Duration: 12 months; 3-month extension possible via 3 months of horticulture/viticulture work
Selectivity: Low — apply online, US scheme uncapped
Status 2026: OPEN to US citizens. Age 18–30.

What It Is: Bilateral Working Holiday Authorisation allowing US citizens to live and work in Ireland for up to 12 months. Applied for through Irish consulates in the US. Requires current enrollment in full-time post-secondary education or graduation within prior 12 months.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: WHA fee $270 (charged by Irish consulate). €300 Irish Residence Permit fee if staying >90 days. Irish minimum wage approximately EUR 13.50/hr in 2026. Hospitality, retail, office work typical. Must show $1,500 in bank. Net positive over 12 months; entry-level hospitality earns EUR 1,800–2,500/mo.
Referral / Partner Economics: No affiliate program. USIT and similar youth travel agencies sell add-on starter packages (accommodation, orientation) for USD $300–600.
Stage: Must be current student or recent grad (within 12 months)
Selectivity: Low — apply by post/in person to consulate; no annual cap published
Status 2026: OPEN to US citizens. Age 18+. Must be in full-time post-secondary education or recent grad.

Program: South Korea Working Holiday Visa (H-1) — US WEST Program
What It Is: Open-work visa for US citizens to live and work in South Korea. US route is the WEST (Work, English Study, Travel) program administered by NIIED/Korean consulate. Unique: no age limit for US citizens, but requires current higher education enrollment or graduation within 1 year.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Visa fee ~USD $45. Annual quota 2,000 for US citizens. Proof of KRW 3,000,000 (~USD $2,200) funds required. Typical wages: service/hospitality KRW 2,000,000–3,000,000/mo; English tutoring at hagwons KRW 2,000,000–2,500,000/mo permitted on H-1 for native English speakers with degree. Max 25 hrs/week for most work types.
Referral / Partner Economics: No formal affiliate. NIIED administers directly. Hagwon recruiters charge employers 1 month's salary (~KRW 2,000,000) placement fee, unpublished to applicants.
Duration: 12 months; not extendable, one per lifetime
Stage: Must be current higher education student or recent grad
Selectivity: Low-Moderate — quota of 2,000/yr for US fills; apply early in annual cycle
Status 2026: OPEN to US citizens. NO age limit for US nationals. Must be enrolled in or recently graduated from higher education.
Source: https://koreaworkexpert.com/working-holiday-h1-visa-korea-2026/ (citing Korean Ministry of Justice March 2026 manual)

What It Is: Highly selective 6-month open-work pass for students/recent grads from 7 countries including USA. Only 2,000 places/year total across all nationalities. Singapore does not have a national minimum wage so market salaries apply.
Participant Pay or Cost 2026: Application IPA: free online. Pass issuance fee SGD $175 (~USD $130). Proof of SGD $2,500 funds required. Office/tech/finance salaries SGD $2,500–4,500/mo (~USD $1,850–3,300). Hospitality SGD $1,800–2,800/mo. No CPF deductions for WHP holders so gross is close to net. Very high-value vs other Asian WHVs.
Referral / Partner Economics: No affiliate program. MOM issues directly; no third-party fee permitted in the application process.
Duration: 6 months; no extension, no second WHP per lifetime
Stage: Must be current university student OR graduate within past 6 months
